metadata.title: A fictional follow-up study of FIC-A

evidence.quote: Our target FIC-A is also designated FIC-001.
Our target FIC-A is also designated FIC-001.
We obtained new spectroscopy of FIC-A because earlier work identified it as a candidate unbound from the Milky Way.
Our new spectroscopy gives a heliocentric radial velocity of 520 ± 10 km/s for FIC-A.
Earlier Study spectroscopy yielded a heliocentric radial velocity of 550 ± 20 km/s for FIC-A.

values.condition: Spectrophotometric estimate using stellar model S

evidence.quote: Our spectrophotometric estimate using stellar model S gives a heliocentric distance of 8.2 kpc for FIC-A, with lower and upper uncertainties of -0.6 and +0.8 kpc.

values.condition: Distance constraint from stellar model T at 95% confidence

evidence.quote: Using stellar model T, we obtain d ≤ 10.0 kpc at 95% confidence for the heliocentric distance of FIC-A.

values.condition: Distance constraint from stellar model U

evidence.quote: Using stellar model U, we find that the heliocentric distance of FIC-A satisfies d > 5.0 kpc.

values.condition: 95% credible interval for the heliocentric distance from stellar model V

evidence.quote: Using stellar model V, we obtain a 95% credible interval of 7.0–9.0 kpc for the heliocentric distance of FIC-A; no central estimate is reported.
Our analysis gives FIC-A a Galactic unbound probability of 95% under Galactic potential Model A.
Our analysis gives FIC-A a Galactic unbound probability of 10% under Galactic potential Model B.

notes: FIC-B was excluded because T:p2-b3 only mentions it as background and reports no qualifying contribution.

FIC-A: T:p4-b2 gives a parallax of 0.25 mas, while T:p4-b3 gives 0.025 mas for the same measurement without explanation; this may be a typographical error, so neither value was included or corrected. The unbound probabilities of 95% and 10% were retained separately because T:p5-b1 and T:p5-b2 explicitly use different Galactic potential models; they were not treated as a numerical conflict.
